summary: Rabbi Soffer concludes the discussion in Masekhet Bechorot regarding the status of animals when a mistake is made during the counting of Maaser Behemah. He explores the opinions of the Hakhamim and Rabbi Yehuda concerning whether such animals are offered as Korbanot or left to graze, and addresses the validity of a Shaliach making a mistake on behalf of an owner. The class concludes with a brief introduction to the laws of Erech vows in Masekhet Arakhin.
questions: What happens if two animals come out of the pen at the same time during the counting of Maaser?
Is it considered an 'Akira' if I call the tenth animal eleven?
Can a Shaliach make a mistake when counting Maaser for someone else?
Why does Rabbi Yehuda hold that a Temura of a Maaser animal might be left to die?
Who is allowed to make an Erech vow?
